transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just feel worn out almost every day. It's like, even after I get a full night's sleep, my body and my head are still just dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Yeah, I do. It feels like... well, my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next. I'll be worrying about money, and then I'll start thinking about the relative we have staying with us, or how stressed my wife has been. Then it's on to my church duties, or... or wondering if I'm messing up at work. It just kind of bounces around like that all the time.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah, it really is. I try telling myself to just pray on it or... or just leave it alone. But it doesn't really work. Once a worry starts, it just keeps rolling right into another one. It's like I can't stop it until I'm sitting there thinking through every bad way the day could go.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or sad. It's not really like that. It's mostly just... the stress of all the worrying, you know? It definitely makes me tired and overwhelmed, but I don't feel down in the dumps or anything.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah, I definitely do. Most nights I get into bed feeling really tired, but then... I just lie there. My mind starts going over the bills, my work schedule, and just worrying about whether everyone at home is okay. It keeps me up. And even when I finally do get some sleep, I usually wake up feeling like I never really settled down or got any actual rest.
Has this kind of ongoing worry been happening for at least six months?

Yeah, definitely longer than six months. I'd say it's been going on for about a year and three months now. That's, um, that's right around the time our older relative moved in with us, and it's just been pretty constant ever since.
Do you often feel muscle tension, like tightness or aching in your neck, shoulders, or back?

No, not really. I mean, my feet get a bit sore sometimes from standing at the register all day, but I haven't noticed any real tightness or aching in my neck or back. So, no, I don't think I have that.
Do you find yourself feeling more irritable than usual?

No, I wouldn't say I'm more irritable. I mean, I get stressed out with all the worrying, but I don't really snap at people or get angry easily. It's more just... internal stress, you know? So, no, not really irritable.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind feels preoccupied with worry?

Yeah, I do actually. Like, when I'm at work at the register, I can be looking right at the screen and still just... lose track of what I'm doing. My mind wanders because I'm thinking about things at home or worrying about bills. And that's when I end up having to recount the drawer or catch a small mistake I made. So yeah, it definitely messes with my focus.
If you are not worrying about anything, do you still have trouble sleeping?
No, I don't think so. If my mind is actually quiet and I'm not stressing over something, I sleep pretty well. I haven't really noticed any problems falling asleep just out of nowhere.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?
No, not really. I mean, my mind is always going with all the worrying, but physically I don't feel restless or anything. I can sit still just fine. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel keyed up.
When you have trouble falling asleep, is it usually because your mind is worrying?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Most nights I get in bed feeling really tired, but then I just lie there going over things. I start thinking about the bills, my work schedule at the store, or just... whether everyone at home is okay. It keeps me awake. And honestly, even when I do finally get to sleep, I usually wake up feeling like I never really settled down or got any real rest.
